1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Nc3 Nf6 4.d4 Bb4 5.N.strategy: Wins the e5 pawn, with the knight supported by the d4 pawn. It is a real gambit all the same: the pinned c3 knight leaves e4 short of defenders, so White takes the pawn at the price of quick counterplay against the centre and the exposed knights.
1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Nc3 Nf6 4.d4 Bb4 5.N.name: Four Knights Game: Scotch Variation, Krause Gambit

1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Nc3 Nf6 4.d4 Bb4 5.d.strategy: Drives the c6 knight away with a gain of space and leaves the e5 pawn undefended. The fight moves from the pawn to the centre: White has more room, Black has the pin on c3 and the loose e4 pawn to work with.

Moves the attacked knight to the centre, where the e5 pawn guards it and where it eyes f3 and c2. Black gives up the e5 pawn for this, which White can take, and relies on the pin and the pressure on e4 and f3 for compensation.
1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Nc3 Nf6 4.d4 Bb4 5.d.name: Four Knights Game: Scotch Variation, Oxford Gambit

1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Nc3 Nf6 4.d4 Bb4 5.N.strategy: Attacks the e5 knight a second time, so that the c6 knight and the queen together outweigh the d4 pawn that guards it, and brings the queen to the e-file. White cannot keep the extra pawn without finding more support for the knight.
1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Nc3 Nf6 4.d4 Bb4 5.N.name: Four Knights Game: Scotch Variation, Krause Gambit, Leonhardt Defence
